easy.def: A word used to show a choice.
examples: Do you want milk or juice?
Is it day or night?
We can walk or ride.

more.def: A word that offers a choice between things, and adds one more possibility.
examples: You can have soup or a salad with your lunch.
Is the whale a fish, or is it a mammal?
Hurry up, or we will miss the bus.

easy.def: A wise person or place in old stories who told the future.
examples: The king asked the oracle.
The oracle gave an answer.
An oracle spoke.

more.def: In ancient stories, a wise person or holy place that gave answers about the future.
examples: The king asked the oracle for advice.
In Greek myths, people traveled far to ask the oracle.
The oracle's answer was a riddle.

easy.def: Said out loud, not written down.
examples: We have an oral test.
She gave an oral report.
He made an oral promise.

more.def: Spoken out loud rather than written down.
examples: We gave an oral report in front of the class.
The teacher gave us an oral quiz instead of a written one.
He made an oral promise to feed the cat.

easy.def: Of the mouth.
examples: Brush your teeth for good oral health.
The dentist gave oral advice.
Oral medicine is taken by mouth.

more.def: Having to do with the mouth.
examples: The dentist talked about oral health and brushing twice a day.
The doctor gave him an oral medicine to take with water.
Brushing is part of good oral care.

easy.def: A round fruit with a thick skin and sweet juice.
examples: I peel an orange.
The orange is juicy.
Oranges grow on trees.

more.def: A round, juicy fruit with a bright skin that grows on trees in warm places.
examples: She peeled the orange and shared the pieces.
Oranges are full of vitamin C.
He squeezed three oranges to make juice.

easy.def: A color that is between red and yellow.
examples: My shirt is orange.
The leaves turn orange in fall.
Orange is a bright color.

more.def: The bright color of a carrot or a pumpkin, between red and yellow.
examples: The sunset turned the sky orange and pink.
Pumpkins are orange in the fall.
She painted the fish bright orange.

easy.def: A large ape with long red hair and long arms.
examples: The orangutan swings.
An orangutan has red hair.
We saw an orangutan at the zoo.

more.def: A large ape with long arms and shaggy red-brown hair that lives in trees.
examples: An orangutan swung from tree to tree.
The orangutan has long, strong arms.
Orangutans live in the forests of Asia.

easy.def: A round ball shape.
examples: The orb glowed.
The moon is an orb.
He held a shiny orb.

more.def: A round object, like a ball, often shiny or glowing.
examples: The glowing orb floated in the dark cave.
The moon hung in the sky like a pale orb.
The king held a golden orb in his hand.

easy.def: To go around and around something in space.
examples: The Earth orbits the sun.
The moon orbits the Earth.
A spaceship orbits the planet.

more.def: To travel in a curved path around a planet, moon, or star.
examples: The moon orbits the Earth about once every month.
Many satellites orbit the Earth and send signals for phones.
It takes one year for the Earth to orbit the sun.

easy.def: A spacecraft that goes around a planet.
examples: The orbiter circled.
An orbiter goes around Mars.
The orbiter takes pictures.

more.def: A space machine that goes around a planet.
examples: The orbiter circled Mars.
An orbiter took pictures of the surface.
The orbiter sent back data.

easy.def: A black and white whale.
examples: An orca is a whale.
The orca jumped.
I saw an orca.

more.def: A large black-and-white whale, also called a killer whale.
examples: An orca leaped from the water.
Orcas travel in family groups.
The orca is a type of dolphin.

easy.def: A place where fruit trees grow.
examples: We picked apples in the orchard.
Pears grow in the orchard.
Birds sing in the orchard.

more.def: A piece of land where fruit or nut trees are grown.
examples: The orchard was full of ripe peaches.
The family runs a cherry orchard.
We walked between rows of trees in the orchard.

easy.def: A large group of musicians.
examples: The orchestra plays.
I heard an orchestra.
The orchestra has violins.

more.def: A large group of musicians who play many kinds of instruments together.
examples: The orchestra played a lively tune.
My sister plays the flute in the orchestra.
The conductor led the orchestra.

easy.def: To arrange the parts of something carefully.
examples: She orchestrated the show.
He orchestrates the event.
They orchestrate music.

more.def: To plan and organize the parts of something so that they work together.
examples: She orchestrated the whole school show.
The teacher orchestrated the field day.
He orchestrated the music for the band.

easy.def: A flower with an unusual shape that comes in many bright colors.
examples: An orchid sat on the table.
The orchid is purple.
Grandma grows an orchid.

more.def: A plant with colorful flowers of unusual shapes, often grown indoors.
examples: Some orchids grow high in the trees of the rainforest.
A pink orchid bloomed on the kitchen windowsill.
The greenhouse was full of orchids in every color.

easy.def: A hard, scary time.
examples: Getting lost was an ordeal.
It was a long ordeal.
The ordeal was over.

more.def: A very hard or painful experience that is hard to get through.
examples: Being lost in the woods overnight was a frightening ordeal.
The long, cold wait was a real ordeal for the hikers.
It was an ordeal for her to give a speech in front of the whole school.

easy.def: The way things are placed one after another.
examples: Put them in order.
The cards are in order.
Say the days in order.

more.def: The way that things are arranged in a line or sequence.
examples: Please put the numbers in order from smallest to biggest.
The books were in alphabetical order on the shelf.
The order of the days is Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday.

easy.def: To ask for food or goods to be sent to you.
examples: We order pizza.
She ordered soup.
I will order a book.

more.def: To ask for food or goods to be made or sent to you.
examples: We ordered a pizza for Friday night.
She ordered a book about frogs from the store.
Dad ordered soup and a sandwich at the cafe.

easy.def: Neat and in the right place.
examples: Her desk is orderly.
The toys are in orderly rows.
We made an orderly line.

more.def: Neat, tidy and arranged in the right order.
examples: The students made an orderly line at the door.
He kept his shelf orderly, with books sorted by size.
The orderly crowd walked out of the hall without pushing.

easy.def: Usually.
examples: I ordinarily walk to school.
It is ordinarily quiet here.
She ordinarily wakes early.

more.def: In the usual way; as a rule.
examples: I ordinarily walk to school, but today it rained.
The park is ordinarily quiet on weekdays.
He ordinarily eats breakfast at seven.

easy.def: Normal; not special.
examples: It was an ordinary day at school.
I wore my ordinary shoes.
He is an ordinary boy who loves soccer.

more.def: Usual or normal; not different or special in any way.
examples: It looked like an ordinary rock, but there was a crystal inside.
On an ordinary morning, I wake up at seven.
The hero of the story is an ordinary girl who does something brave.

easy.def: Rock with metal in it.
examples: Miners dig up ore.
Iron ore is red.
The ore has gold.

more.def: Rock or earth that contains a useful metal, such as iron or gold.
examples: Miners dug iron ore out of the mountain.
The ore is heated in a furnace to get the metal out.
The ore sparkled with tiny bits of gold.

easy.def: A herb used in pizza and pasta sauce.
examples: The pizza has oregano.
Oregano smells good.
I sprinkled oregano.

more.def: A leafy herb used to flavor pizza and pasta sauces.
examples: Mom sprinkled oregano on the pizza.
Oregano grows in our herb garden.
The sauce smelled of tomato and oregano.

easy.def: A part of the body that does a job.
examples: The heart is an organ.
Your lungs are organs.
The organ pumps blood.

more.def: A part of the body that does a special job, such as the heart or lungs.
examples: The heart is an organ that pumps blood.
Your lungs and kidneys are organs.
The brain is the body's main organ.

easy.def: A large musical instrument with pipes and keys.
examples: The organ is in the church.
He plays the organ.
The organ sounds deep.

more.def: A big musical instrument with pipes and a keyboard that makes a deep, rich sound.
examples: The organ in the church played a slow song.
He practiced on the pipe organ.
The organ filled the hall with deep music.

easy.def: Grown without chemicals.
examples: The apples are organic.
We buy organic food.
The farm is organic.

more.def: Grown or made without man-made chemicals, or coming from living things.
examples: The farmer grew organic vegetables without using chemicals to kill bugs.
We bought organic milk from a local farm.
Compost is organic material made from old leaves and food scraps.

easy.def: Any living thing.
examples: A tree is an organism.
Bacteria are tiny organisms.
A fish is an organism.

more.def: A living thing, such as a plant, an animal or a tiny life form too small to see.
examples: Every plant and animal is an organism that needs food and air to live.
Scientists use a microscope to study tiny organisms in pond water.
A mushroom is an organism that is neither a plant nor an animal.

easy.def: A person who plays the organ.
examples: The organist played.
An organist plays music.
The organist sat at the organ.

more.def: A person who plays the organ, a big keyboard instrument.
examples: The organist played a hymn.
An organist uses both hands and feet.
The organist sat at the church organ.

easy.def: A group of people who work together for a purpose.
examples: The organization helps animals.
She works for a big organization.
The organization raised money.

more.def: A group of people who join together to do something, such as a club or business.
examples: The organization helps animals find homes.
She works for an organization that cleans rivers.
The organization raised money for the school.

easy.def: To put things in order.
examples: Let's organize the toys by color.
I organize my crayons.
We organized a bake sale.

more.def: To arrange things in a neat order, or to plan an event.
examples: We organized the books by author on the shelf.
The students organized a clean-up day at the park.
She organized her notes before the test.

easy.def: A person or tool that puts things in order.
examples: The organizer planned the party.
A desk organizer holds pens.
The organizer is neat.

more.def: A person who plans an event, or a tool for keeping things in order.
examples: The organizer planned the school fair.
A desk organizer holds pens and tape.
She is an organizer who keeps everything on time.

easy.def: The art of folding paper into shapes.
examples: I made origami.
Origami uses paper.
She folds origami cranes.

more.def: The Japanese art of folding paper into shapes such as birds and flowers.
examples: She folded a paper crane using origami.
Origami needs only paper and careful folds.
We made origami boats in art class.

easy.def: Where something comes from.
examples: What is the origin of the word?
The origin of the river.
The origin is Greece.

more.def: The place or time where something starts.
examples: What is the origin of this word?
The origin of the river is in the mountains.
Pizza has its origin in Italy.

easy.def: First or new.
examples: The original plan.
My original idea.
An original painting.

more.def: Existing first, or new and not copied.
examples: The original plan was to meet at noon.
She wrote an original song.
The museum has the original painting.

related.def: Not new; copied from something else.

easy.def: Being new and different.
examples: I like her originality.
The story has originality.
Show originality.

more.def: The quality of being new and different, not copied.
examples: I admire the originality of her drawings.
The story is full of originality.
The teacher praised the originality of his idea.

easy.def: At first.
examples: The house was originally red.
I was originally from Texas.
It was originally a barn.

more.def: At the beginning, before things changed.
examples: The house was originally painted red.
My family is originally from Texas.
The building was originally a barn.

easy.def: To start or come from a place.
examples: The game originated in Asia.
Where did this originate?
Fire can originate from a spark.

more.def: To begin or come from a certain place or person.
examples: The game of chess is thought to have originated in India.
The river originates high in the mountains.
The idea originated with a student in our class.

easy.def: A bright orange and black bird.
examples: An oriole sang.
The oriole is orange.
I saw an oriole.

more.def: A songbird with bright orange and black feathers that builds a hanging nest.
examples: An oriole sang from the treetop.
The oriole built a hanging nest.
Orioles eat fruit and insects.

easy.def: A pretty thing used to decorate something.
examples: We hung an ornament on the tree.
The ornament is shiny.
She made an ornament.

more.def: A small, pretty object that is used to decorate a room or a tree.
examples: We hung a glass ornament on the Christmas tree.
She put a small ornament on the shelf.
The ornament was shaped like a star.

easy.def: Used for looks, not for use.
examples: The pond has ornamental fish.
It is an ornamental tree.
An ornamental lamp.

more.def: Used as a decoration, to look nice rather than to be useful.
examples: The garden had an ornamental pond with goldfish.
The ornamental lamp was just for show.
They planted ornamental cherry trees along the road.

easy.def: Covered with lots of fancy shapes.
examples: The ornate clock was gold.
She wore an ornate crown.
The ornate door had flowers carved on it.

more.def: Decorated with many fancy details and shapes.
examples: The palace had an ornate ceiling painted with gold and blue.
An ornate frame surrounded the old painting.
The ornate gate was carved with leaves and flowers.

easy.def: Cross and hard to deal with.
examples: The ornery mule would not move.
An ornery old man.
The ornery goat.

more.def: Bad-tempered and stubborn.
examples: The ornery mule refused to move.
An ornery old goat chased the children.
He was ornery before breakfast.

easy.def: A scientist who studies birds.
examples: The ornithologist watched birds.
An ornithologist loves birds.
She is an ornithologist.

more.def: A scientist who studies birds.
examples: The ornithologist watched birds through binoculars.
An ornithologist records bird songs.
She became an ornithologist.

easy.def: The study of birds.
examples: She studies ornithology.
Ornithology is about birds.
He likes ornithology.

more.def: The scientific study of birds.
examples: She studies ornithology and watches birds.
Ornithology teaches us about bird songs.
He wants to work in ornithology.

easy.def: A child whose parents have died.
examples: The orphan lived with her aunt.
The orphan was adopted.
The book is about an orphan.

more.def: A child whose mother and father have both died.
examples: The orphan lived with her aunt and uncle.
The story is about an orphan who finds a home.
The kind family adopted the orphan.

easy.def: A home for children who have no parents.
examples: The orphanage was big.
The children lived at the orphanage.
A kind woman ran the orphanage.

more.def: A place where children who have no parents live and are cared for.
examples: She grew up in an orphanage until she was adopted.
The orphanage was a big brick house.
The orphanage had a garden and a playroom.

easy.def: A dentist who straightens teeth.
examples: The orthodontist gave me braces.
An orthodontist fixes teeth.
I go to the orthodontist.

more.def: A dentist who specializes in straightening teeth, often with braces.
examples: An orthodontist uses wires to move teeth into place.
An orthodontist checks how your teeth line up.
I go to the orthodontist every month.
